title: Capacity runway scenarios & cumulative unit-cost workbook
body:
Purpose:
This workbook captures a compact, model-ready set of capacity-runway scenarios and cumulative unit-cost calculations to feed the Optimize recommendations engine. Goal is to produce per-scenario monthly outputs: (1) compute capacity needed, (2) expected infra cost (reserved vs burst), (3) per-token and per-request unit cost after amortization and batching gains, (4) headroom runway in months.

Summary of approach (short):
- Build 3 scenario families: Baseline (steady growth), Surge (short high-growth episodes), Enterprise Ramp (sustained large accounts onboarding).
- For each month, compute: QPS demand, avg tokens/req, tokens/day, avg concurrency, required GPU hours (with packing/batching assumptions), reserve commit sizing, burst (on-demand/spot) hours, prewarm/warmup costs, and resulting per-token cost.
- Include simple sensitivity knobs: batching factor, KV cache hit rate, quantization delta (FP16 vs 4-bit), and reserved discount.

Key high-level assumptions (editable):
- Avg sequence length (tokens): Baseline 64, Surge 80, Enterprise 120
- Requests per second (starting month 0): Baseline 200 QPS, Surge 500 QPS peak, Enterprise 1200 QPS at peak
- Working days considered: 30 days/month
- GPU profile: A40-equivalent, sustained throughput ~1200 tokens/sec with avg seq 64 under baseline packing model
- GPU hourly cost (on-demand): $2.50/hr (cloud list). Reserved hourly cost (committed): $1.60/hr (committed discount). Spot/interruptible: $0.90/hr (available but with 20% preemption assumption)
- Packing/batching effective throughput gain: batching factor (config) defaults to 1.8x under modern runtime (continuous batching).
- KV cache hit: default 15% for chat workloads (reduces token compute count by cached prefix tokens)
- Prewarm GPUs per pool: assume 10% of peak concurrent allocation retained warm for latency SLOs with an amortized 24hr prewarm cost
- SLO-driven tail margin: +10% capacity for latency headroom (targets p95)

Scenario table (example month snapshot) - columns explained below:
Month,Scenario,QPS,AvgTokens,TokensPerDay,BatchFactor,CacheHit,EffectiveTokensPerGPUperHr,RequiredGPUhrs,ReservedHours,BurstHours,PrewarmHours,TotalInfraCost,AmortizedPerTokenCost
M06,Baseline,320,64,1,3820800,1.8,4,4000,3000,1000,480,
(Notes: TokensPerDay = QPS * 86400 * AvgTokens; EffectiveTokensPerGPUperHr = base_throughput * BatchFactor * (1 - CacheHit); RequiredGPUhrs = ceil((TokensPerDay / EffectiveTokensPerGPUperHr) / 24) * 24 )

Example filled values (month M06 baseline, numeric):
M06,Baseline,320,64,1,17694720,1.8,1029600,720,560,160,80,
Computed steps for the example numeric row:
- Tokens/day = 320 QPS * 86400 sec/day * 64 tokens = 1,766,40,?? wait compute properly: 320*86400=27,648,000 requests? Actually QPS * sec * tokens = tokens/day -> 320*86400*64 = 1,769,472,000 tokens/day (this sheet keeps raw tokens large to ensure correct denom in amortization).
- Base GPU throughput (tokens/sec) with avg seq 64 = 1200 toks/sec => per hour 4,320,000 tokens/hr. With batching factor 1.8x => 7,776,000 toks/hr. After 15% KV hit => effective 6,609,600 toks/hr.
- Required GPU hours/day = tokens/day / effective_tokens_per_hour => 1,769,472,000 / 6,609,600 = 267.6 GPU-hours/day => monthly GPU-hours = 267.6*30 = 8,028 GPU-hrs/month. Then apply SLO margin +10% => 8,830 GPU-hrs/month -> round up to 8,840.

Capacity split logic (per month):
- ReservedHours = min(commit_size, RequiredGPUhrs * 0.8) (we don't commit more than 80% of predicted need; remainder on burst)
- BurstHours = RequiredGPUhrs - ReservedHours (plus any prewarm allocated as separate line item)
- PrewarmHours = ReservedHours * 0.1 (cells assume 10% of reserved remain warm 24x)

Cost calculations (cells):
- ReservedCost = ReservedHours * reserved_hourly_rate
- BurstCost = BurstHours * spot_hourly_rate * (1 + preemption overhead 0.05) + OnDemandFallbackHours * on_demand_rate
- PrewarmCost = PrewarmHours * reserved_hourly_rate * 24/30 (amortize daily warm instances across month)
- TotalInfraCost = ReservedCost + BurstCost + PrewarmCost + network/ebs overhead (default 5% of compute cost)
- AmortizedPerTokenCost = TotalInfraCost / TokensPerMonth (TokensPerMonth = TokensPerDay * 30)

Sensitivity grid (what to run):
- sweep BatchFactor: [1.2, 1.5, 1.8, 2.2]
- sweep KV cache hit: [0.05, 0.15, 0.30]
- sweep Reserved discount: [10%, 30%, 40%] (changes reserved_hourly_rate)
- sweep AvgTokens: add a row for +20% and -20% seq length impact

Stress tests to export for Optimize engine (CSV):
- 12-month monthly rows for each scenario with columns: month, qps, avg_tokens, tokens_month, req_gpu_hrs, reserved_hrs, burst_hrs, prewarm_hrs, reserved_cost, burst_cost, prewarm_cost, total_cost, per_token_cost
- tags: scenario-id and tags for batch experiment mapping (e.g., optimize-experiment-2026-02-runA)

Recommendations (first-pass, actionable):
- Short term (next 3 months): commit to a small reserved footprint equal to 30% of predicted peak for Baseline to capture committed discounts while keeping flexibility. Increase KV cache TTL for chat workloads and push prompt templating to reduce avg tokens by ~6-8% (estimated 0.04 token reduction per request).
- Medium term (3-9 months): Introduce a two-tier reserved pool: fast-warm (p95 latency) ~10% peak on reserved, and cold reserved for batch throughput. This lets reduce prewarm costs and improve utilization. Target reserved discounts at >= 30% in negotiations for Dedicated contracts.
- Long term (9-12 months): Add model quantization/half-swap profiles for stable enterprise traffic (quantize to 4-bit where acceptable) — model delta reduces required GPU-hours by ~1.4x. Build automated rollout triggers in Optimize to switch model variants when downstream QA metrics are in range.

Open questions / TODOs (quick):
- Validate base GPU throughput per model variant under realistic seq-length distributions (need bench runs: bench-run-2026-02-18).
- Confirm spot availability and region-level preemption rates (cloud provider SRE ask).
- Add per-request tail latency cost model (cold-start penalty) to better size prewarm pool.
